question: A 42-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of tingling in his hands and legs and palpitations for 1 week. He has also had severe cramping in his hands, feet, and abdomen during this period. Three months ago, he was hospitalized for acute pancreatitis. He discharged himself against medical advice at that time. There is no family history of illness. He does not smoke. He drinks 2–3 beers and a pint of vodka daily. He has a history of using intravenous heroin. He has not had a stable job for a year. He is only oriented to place and person. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/96 mm Hg. There is a carpopedal spasm while measuring his blood pressure. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with tingling in hands and legs" -> "Symptoms suggest possible electrolyte imbalance" -> "History of alcohol use indicates potential magnesium deficiency" -> "Carpopedal spasm suggests hypomagnesemia" -> "Magnesium sulfate is indicated for treatment" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of acute pancreatitis" -> "Pancreatitis can lead to malabsorption of nutrients" -> "Malabsorption may cause electrolyte imbalances" -> "Severe cramping and spasms indicate possible hypocalcemia or hypomagnesemia" -> "Magnesium sulfate is appropriate for treating hypomagnesemia" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient exhibits 4+ deep tendon reflexes" -> "Hyperreflexia can indicate electrolyte disturbances" -> "Tingling and cramping suggest neuromuscular irritability" -> "Alcohol use can lead to magnesium depletion" -> "Magnesium sulfate is a suitable treatment option" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient is oriented to place and person" -> "Cognitive function is somewhat preserved" -> "Neurologic examination shows no focal findings" -> "Symptoms are likely due to systemic issues rather than a primary neurological disorder" -> "Magnesium sulfate can help address systemic electrolyte issues" -> 70%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of electrolyte imbalances, particularly hypomagnesemia, which can cause carpopedal spasms and increased deep tendon reflexes. Given his history of alcohol use and potential malnutrition, magnesium deficiency is likely. Therefore, magnesium sulfate is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy to address his symptoms.
